name: h Ursae Majoris
description: A naked-eye star 23.8 parsecs away, 2.9 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.133 +/- 0.009 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 2.902 +/- 0.026

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.824 +/- 0.016

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6693 +/- 45

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 41.99 +/- 0.16 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 24 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 2.9 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.133 milliarcseconds, which gives 2.902 solar radii and 6,693 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 81937: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
